title: Verbs: 想 vs 要, 应该, 会 (will), 没办法, verb + 一下, double objects
description: Would like (想) vs want (要), should, will, can't (no way), doing something briefly, and verbs with two objects.

points.title: 想 vs 要
points.summary: 想 + verb = would like to (softer); 想 + person/place = miss. 要 + noun = want (to have); 要 + verb = want to / be going to (stronger).
points.body:
- 我**想**家 (I'm homesick).
- 我**要**一杯茶 — not ~~我想一杯茶~~.

points.title: 应该 / 该 + verb: should
points.summary: 应该 (yīnggāi) = should, ought to. 该…了 = it's time to ….
points.body:
- 你病了，**应该**多休息.
- 十点了，我**该**走**了**.

points.title: 会 + verb: will (likely)
points.summary: 会 also predicts: it will / is likely to happen. Often with 的 at the end for certainty.
points.body:
- 明天**会**下雨吗?
- 他一定**会**来**的**.

points.title: 没办法 + verb: can't (no way)
points.summary: 没(有)办法 = there's no way to / nothing can be done.
points.body: - 我今天很忙，**没办法**陪你去.
examples: There's no way I can help you.

points.title: Verb + 一下 / verb-verb: briefly
points.summary: Verb + 一下 or doubling the verb (看看, 试试) softens it: 'have a quick …'.
points.body:
- 请等**一下**.
- 你**试试**这件衣服吧.
examples: Why don't you try this on.

points.title: Verb + person + thing (double objects)
points.summary: 给, 教, 问, 告诉 … take the person first, then the thing.
points.body:
- 他给了**我一本书**.
- 老师问了**我们一个问题**.

questions.prompt:
A：{你|nǐ}{想|xiǎng}{喝|hē}{什么|shénme}？
B：{我|wǒ}（　）{一|yì}{杯|bēi}{茶|chá}。
notes: 想 + noun means 'miss' — 'I miss a cup of tea'.
questions.translation: A: What would you like to drink? B: A cup of tea, please.
I've been in China for half a year and I'm really homesick.

notes: 会多休息 = 'will rest more' — a prediction, not advice.
还是 would need a different structure.
questions.translation: You're ill — you should rest more.
It's already ten — time for me to go home.

questions.prompt: {你|nǐ}{看|kàn}，{天|tiān}{这么|zhème}{黑|hēi}，{明天|míngtiān}（　）{下雨|xià yǔ}{吗|ma}？
questions.translation: Look how dark the sky is — will it rain tomorrow?

notes: 一定可以来的 isn't natural.
办法 is a noun — negate it with 没.
没法办 = 'it can't be dealt with'.
questions.translation: I'm really busy today — I can't go with you.

notes: The order is 没有办法.
没办法 comes before the verb.
办法 is a noun — 没, not 不.
questions.translation: There's no way I can help you.
Please wait a moment, he'll be right here.

notes: 试一 is incomplete — 试一试 or 试一下.
一试 can't stand alone here.
questions.translation: This dress is lovely — why don't you try it on.

notes: The person comes before the thing.
The thing can't go before the verb like this.
The person comes after the verb.

questions.prompt: {上课|shàngkè}{的|de}{时候|shíhou}，{老师|lǎoshī}（　）{我们|wǒmen}{一个|yí ge}{问题|wèntí}。
notes: 说 doesn't take a person as the first object.
questions.translation: In class, the teacher asked us a question.
